_about: Synthetic review cases. Each case points at one row of S8.synthetic_cashy_sample.csv (0-based data row). The interviewer's view, transcript, Cashy's reasoning and Cashy's answer are authored placeholders until a Cashy-like model produces them. No real household. Reasoning 'agree' = reasons to include the household, 'disagree' = reasons to exclude it.

interviewer_view: Head of household is a woman caring alone for her 9-year-old son and her mother, who has diabetes. They stay in a temporary shelter that allows them one more month.
She cleans houses when someone calls. A cousin abroad occasionally sends small amounts of money. She seemed under strain but was consistent across questions. Food looks like the most pressing need.

transcript.text: Can you tell me who lives with you?
We are three: me, my son, he is nine, and my mother.
My mother has diabetes. We can't always buy her insulin.
Does anyone in the household work?
I clean houses when someone calls me, maybe two days a week.
The shelter lets us stay one more month. After that we don't know.
Some days we skip dinner so my son can eat.
My cousin sometimes sends a little money from the north.
I can't read well. My mother helps me with the forms.
Do you have your identity documents?
Yes, all three of us have our papers.
Last month I sold my phone to pay for her medicine.
Is there anything else you want us to know?
Only that my son needs to go back to school.

agree: The head of household is the sole carer of a 9-year-old child and her mother, who has a chronic illness and requires ongoing treatment.
The household is in a precarious housing situation, with the shelter stay ending soon and no stable accommodation after that.
Basic needs are not being met: the family is skipping meals and the mother sold personal belongings to pay for medical care.
Limited literacy and weak access to services increase the household's vulnerability and reduce its ability to cope independently.
disagree: The household receives regular income from a relative abroad.
An adult has paid work, about two days a week.
Documents are complete and an adult speaks Spanish, which eases access to work.

cashy.certainty_text: Low. Of past households like this one, about 5 in 10 were included.

interviewer_view: Single adult, 61 years old, travelling alone with no relatives in the country. Rents a shared room and earns from street sales, which currently cover rent and food.
Cannot read or write. Calm and consistent. Needs look covered for now, but the income is irregular and the respondent borrowed to pay rent last month.

transcript.text: Who is travelling with you?
Nobody. I came alone. I am sixty-one.
I rent a room that I share with two other people. It is paid until the end of next month.
Are you able to eat every day?
Yes. On weekdays I have lunch at the community kitchen.
I sell sweets on the street most days. It pays the rent and the food.
Last month I borrowed from a neighbour to pay the rent on time.
I cannot read or write. Could you read me the form?
Do you have your documents?
Yes, I have my papers. I am healthy, thank God.

agree: An older adult travelling alone, with no support network in the country.
Cannot read or write, which limits access to services and formal work.
Has started borrowing to cover rent, a sign that the income is not always enough.
disagree: Basic needs are met. The respondent eats every day, with lunch at a community kitchen on weekdays.
Street sales cover rent and food.
Housing is secured until the end of next month in a rented room.
No health conditions or specific needs are reported.

cashy.certainty_text: High. Of past households like this one, about 1 in 10 were included.
